title: Deputy Director General Information Systems
description:
Deputy Director General Information Systems
General Information
Type of contract

Fixed-term contract which may be converted into a permanent contract after five years subject to individual performance and organisational needs
Who can apply?

EU nationals
Salary

K full time monthly net salary: €12,510 plus benefits, for further information see

what we offer.
Role specialisation

Leadership
Working time

Full time
Place of work

Frankfurt am Main, Germany
Closing date

28.10.2026
Your team

You will be part of the senior management team in the Directorate General Information Systems, which comprises around 350 members of staff developing, delivering and supporting information and communication systems and information technology (IT) services for our users in the ECB, ECB Banking Supervision, the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) and beyond.

We deliver stable IT services and lead IT projects in close collaboration with business stakeholders and external partners in the areas of end-user computing, networking, IT system and cloud services, security operations, application development, and support and maintenance. We also provide IT governance services (including IT architecture and IT security policies) for the common systems and services of the Eurosystem and the ESCB. We lead the IT Committee, which includes representatives from the ECB and national central banks, and actively participate in its substructures and working groups.

The ECB is an inclusive employer and we strive to reflect the diversity of the population we serve. We encourage you to apply irrespective of age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religious beliefs, sexual orientation or other characteristics.
Your role

As Deputy Director General Information Systems, you will serve as a strategic technology leader at the heart of the ECB's digital transformation, operating at an executive level. You will:

- provide, together with the Director General, strategic direction and leadership for activities within your business area, including defining the overall strategy and setting the strategic direction, managing staff, medium-term planning, budgeting, resource allocation, and other relevant tasks;
- play a key role in developing future technology leaders and strengthening organisational technology capabilities across the Directorate General;
- oversee the delivery of major IT projects and services to achieve the ECB’s business objectives, including operational resilience and strategic autonomy;
- oversee critical technology capabilities while leading the adoption of modern technologies such as cloud computing, artificial intelligence, data platforms, and development, security and operations practices;
- ensure the provision of timely and effective IT services, creating measurable business value across the ECB;
- foster the Directorate General’s ongoing cultural, organisational and technological transformation, such as cloud-based solutions, development and operations (DevOps), and agile working;
- promote a collaborative working environment and an engaged, agile and healthy workforce, and leverage diversity in pursuing business goals;
- align efforts and initiatives regarding the business area’s role in contributing to the strategic direction of the ECB and the Eurosystem/ESCB as a member of the ECB’s senior management team;
- foster close collaboration with other areas of the ECB and with external partners in the areas of end-user computing, networking, IT systems and cloud services, security operations, application development, and support and maintenance;
- represent the Directorate General and the ECB by participating in and/or chairing a wide range of internal and external committees, working groups and high-level fora, and maintaining good working relationships with strategic IT partners.

For this role roles we are seeking candidates who demonstrate the potential for growth, and we will support the selected candidate in their development of the required skills.

We actively support professional development for our staff. Besides learning opportunities, such as training and mentoring, we encourage horizontal mobility after some years in the same position.

The position offers excellent opportunities to drive innovation within a European institution while ensuring the delivery of stable, secure and resilient IT services. It will also enable you to build strong professional networks across Europe and the wider international community. You will be part of a multicultural team that strives for continuous innovation to make a positive impact on the lives of European citizens.
Qualifications, experience and skills

Essential:

- a master’s degree or equivalent in information technology, computer science, computer engineering, physics, mathematics or a related discipline (see How you can join us for details on degree equivalences);
- in addition to the above, a minimum of ten years’ relevant professional experience in leading the successful delivery of large-scale IT projects, having worked in information systems, technology management or a related field;
- at least five years’ experience in managerial roles leading diverse teams;
- significant experience in managing complex technology portfolios and external strategic vendors;
- substantial experience defining and executing enterprise technology strategies involving cloud computing, cybersecurity, data, artificial intelligence and digital/DevOps transformations;
- proven experience balancing innovation, operational resilience, cyber security and regulatory requirements;
- a proven track record of building strong relationships and successful partnerships with business;
- an advanced (C1) command of English and an intermediate (B1) command of at least one other official language of the EU, according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

Desired:

- experience in the financial sector, public sector or highly regulated environments;
- experience in digital sovereignty, critical infrastructure or strategic technology autonomy initiatives.

You build and maintain relationships throughout the organisation and beyond. You emphasise the overarching mission and common aims to achieve the best outcome for the organisation. You strive to achieve goals. You define the strategic outlook for your own business area. You build diverse teams and foster an environment of creativity and innovation. You endeavour to strengthen your teams’ capability, encouraging commitment and engagement.

You are highly motivated to guide teams in their daily work and support their professional development. You are motivated to contribute to the ECB’s mission, to serve the citizens of the EU as a member of a public institution and to work with colleagues from all over Europe.
Working modalities

We would be happy to discuss a part-time arrangement for this role.
Further information

For additional information on this specific vacancy, you can speak to the hiring manager, Alain Busac, at alain.busac@ecb.europa.eu.
Application and selection process

The recruitment process for this position will be conducted onsite. It will include a presentation and interviews (tentatively scheduled from 7 to 15 December).

The selection procedure will also include a separate assessment of your leadership competencies.

If you are not selected for this position but are still considered suitable, you will be placed on a reserve list (see step 4 of How we hire), from which you might be considered for similar positions within the ECB.

title: Team Lead in Market Operations Innovation Lab
description:
Team Lead in Market Operations Innovation Lab
General Information
Type of contract

Fixed-term contract, which may be extended subject to individual performance and organisational needs
Who can apply?

EU nationals
Salary

H (bracket 1 - step 1) full time monthly net salary: €8,318 plus benefits, for further information see

what we offer.
Role specialisation

Market Ops Policy & Implementation
Working time

Full time
Place of work

Frankfurt am Main, Germany
Closing date

02.11.2026
Your team

You will be part of the Market Operations Solutions and Innovations (MSI) Division in the Directorate General Market Operations (DG/M). Our Division has approximately 40 staff. We are responsible for supporting, maintaining and developing applications for market operations and leading innovation and data analytics across DG/M.

In your role as Team Lead you will be part of the Market Operations Innovation Lab (MOSIL). This team of 12 staff members is responsible for data analytics and innovation, and works closely with colleagues in DG/M and the Directorate General Information Systems (DG/IS).
Your role

As Team Lead you will:

- lead MOSIL, delivering innovation, automation and data analytics solutions that enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of DG/M processes;
- coordinate a portfolio of initiatives using the tools, programming languages and data visualisation platforms available within the ECB to address DG/M business needs;
- engage and collaborate with stakeholders across DG/M, DG/IS, other ECB business areas and external partners to build synergies, share know-how and identify opportunities for reuse and innovation;
- drive the exploration of new technologies, including artificial intelligence, and assess their potential application in DG/M in a pragmatic and responsible manner;
- foster a culture of experimentation, collaboration and continuous learning within the team, supporting staff development and cross-team knowledge-sharing;
- contribute to robust data governance for DG/M’s portfolio of applications, including the Market Operations Database (MOPDB) containing Market Operations data and used for analytic purposes.

For this role we are seeking candidates who demonstrate potential for growth, and we will support the selected candidate in developing the required skills. The position offers you excellent opportunities to focus on using technology to bring about innovation and create intrinsic value for DG/M. We actively support professional development for our staff. Besides learning opportunities such as training and mentoring, we encourage and support horizontal mobility after some years in the same position.
Qualifications, experience and skills

Essential:

- a master’s degree or equivalent in economics, finance, business administration or STEM (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) or another relevant field (see How you can join us for details on degree equivalences);
- in addition to the above, a minimum of six years’ relevant professional experience (excluding internships and traineeships) in the field of market operations or closely related areas;
- a sound understanding of technology, including cloud computing, cybersecurity, data analytics, data visualisation, distributed ledger technology and coding;
- a track record of implementing artificial intelligence solutions;
- professional experience in managing innovative activities/projects with a focus on results;
- strong stakeholder management skills, including the ability to translate business needs into practical technology-enabled solutions and work effectively with IT, business and control functions.
- an advanced (C1) command of English and an intermediate (B1) command of at least one other official language of the EU, according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

Desired:

- professional experience in leading or coordinating people working on innovation, automation or data analytics;

You engage collaboratively with others. You pursue team goals and learn willingly from other people’s diverse perspectives. You signal any need for change by explaining it and proposing alternative solutions. You analyse complex information effectively and can evaluate different views to arrive at solutions. You know and anticipate stakeholder needs. You are skilled at encouraging people to develop their abilities and are able to build high-performing teams.

You are motivated to be part of our team and to develop and use your skills and competencies to achieve the aims of this position. You are highly motivated to guide teams in their daily work and support their professional development.
Working modalities

To enable the division to maintain its business continuity capability, you will occasionally be expected to perform work during non-standard working hours and work at the ECB’s standby sites.

We would be happy to discuss a part-time arrangement for this role.
Further information

The contract offered will be fixed-term, the appointment being for 18 months as of the exact starting date of the selected candidate.

Temporary appointments may be extended or made permanent subject to organisational needs and budgetary constraints. This may result in a staff member with a non-convertible fixed-term contract being offered a convertible contract in accordance with the ECB Conditions of Employment.

For additional information on this specific vacancy, you can speak to the hiring manager, Colm Toolin, on +49 69 1344 7719 between 16:00 and 17:00 on Monday, 19 October.
Application and selection process

The recruitment process for this position will be conducted in part remotely. It will include a written exercise, a presentation and an interview.

If you are not selected for this position but are still considered suitable, you will be placed on a reserve list (see step 4 of How we hire), from which you might be considered for similar positions within the ECB.
